question: Assume today is 2026-08-15. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the number of recreation visits to Yellowstone National Park in August 2026, as it will be reported in the National Park Service's official monthly visitation statistics.

target.what: Recreation visits to Yellowstone National Park as reported in the National Park Service's official monthly visitation statistics (NPS Visitor Use Statistics). A recreation visit is one person entering the park for recreational purposes; the same person entering multiple times on separate occasions c
target.publisher: National Park Service (NPS), Visitor Use Statistics program
target.cadence: Monthly, typically published 4–8 weeks after the end of the month
target.caveats: The target period is future relative to the 2026-08-15 cutoff; only partial August 2026 data (if any) would be available. The NPS monthly report may be revised later. candidates.hypothesis: August is consistently the peak month for Yellowstone visitation. The August 2026 value can be estimated by applying the recent year-over-year growth rate or a stable seasonal share to the most recent August value (e.g., August 2025) and adjusting for any known shocks.
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly recreation visit counts for Yellowstone for August 2019–2025, and year-to-date totals for 2026 through July (if available). Also any NPS press releases or preliminary reports for August 2026. Minimum evidence: August 2025 value and the 2026 year-to-date trend.

candidates.hypothesis: Yellowstone's August visitation is a relatively stable share of total NPS August visitation or of visitation to a comparable set of large western parks. If total NPS August 2026 or a proxy is available, the share can be applied.
candidates.data_to_find: Total NPS recreation visits for August 2025 and any preliminary August 2026 data; Yellowstone's share of that total in recent Augusts. Alternatively, visitation to Grand Teton, Glacier, and other nearby parks for August 2025 and 2026 to assess regional trends.

candidates.perspective: Entrance station counts and vehicle occupancy
candidates.hypothesis: Recreation visits can be estimated from the number of vehicles entering the park multiplied by average occupancy. Entrance station counts may be available from park records or traffic counters.
candidates.data_to_find: Average daily vehicle entries at Yellowstone entrances in August (from NPS or DOT traffic data), and average persons per vehicle (from surveys or NPS reports). Minimum evidence: total August vehicle entries and occupancy rate.

candidates.hypothesis: Overnight stays and campground occupancy provide a lower bound or component of total visits. Total visits = overnight visitors + day-use visitors. Overnight capacity and occupancy rates can estimate the overnight component; day-use can be estimated from parking capacity and turnover.
candidates.data_to_find: Number of lodging units and campground sites in Yellowstone, average August occupancy rates, average length of stay, and day-use parking capacity and turnover. Minimum evidence: total overnight capacity and August occupancy.

candidates.hypothesis: Any major closures (e.g., road washouts, wildfires, government shutdown) or policy changes (e.g., reservation requirements) in August 2026 would alter visitation relative to the historical baseline. The direction and magnitude of the effect can be estimated from past similar events.
candidates.data_to_find: News of Yellowstone closures or access restrictions in August 2026, wildfire activity, weather anomalies, and any reservation system changes. Also historical impact of the 2022 flood and 2019 government shutdown on August visitation.

candidates.hypothesis: National or regional tourism forecasts for summer 2026 may indicate whether travel to Yellowstone is expected to be higher or lower than 2025. These forecasts can adjust the baseline estimate.
candidates.data_to_find: Summer 2026 travel forecasts for national parks or the Mountain West, airline bookings to Bozeman/Jackson, and any NPS or Department of Interior visitation projections. Minimum evidence: a directional forecast with quantified expected change.

candidates.hypothesis: Online attention (Google Trends, social media mentions) for Yellowstone in August 2026 relative to August 2025 may correlate with visitation changes. This can serve as a leading indicator if a stable relationship exists.
candidates.data_to_find: Google Trends index for 'Yellowstone National Park' for August 2025 and August 2026 (if available), and social media post volumes. Minimum evidence: relative change in attention.

candidates.hypothesis: August typically accounts for a stable percentage of Yellowstone's annual visitation (e.g., around 15–20%). If a preliminary annual total for 2026 is available or can be forecast, the August share can be applied.
candidates.data_to_find: Yellowstone annual visitation totals for 2019–2025 and the August share each year. Also any 2026 annual forecast or year-to-date total through July to project the annual total.

methods.rationale: Top-down route: NPS-wide 2025 recreation visits (p34) times Yellowstone's August share of NPS-wide August visits (a1) times a year-over-year change factor for NPS-wide August visits (a2). This uses the only kept NPS-wide total and two explicit transfer assumptions. Shared dependencies: both a1 and a2 are assumptions, so the interval width is driven by their uncertainty; the method fails if Yellowstone's August share or the 2026 NPS-wide August level deviates materially from the assumed ranges. It does not use any Yellowstone-specific August history, which is a key limitation.

assumptions.name: Yellowstone August 2026 share of NPS-wide August 2026 recreation visits
assumptions.rationale: Yellowstone is one of the largest parks but its August share of total NPS recreation visits is small. In 2025 Yellowstone's annual visits were roughly 4.7 million (not directly in the kept points but consistent with its Top-10 ranking) against NPS-wide 323 million, implying an annual share near 1.5%. August is a peak month for Yellowstone, so its August share is likely somewhat above its annual share. A central value of 1.2% with a wide range 0.8-1.8% reflects this uncertainty and the lack of a direct August share observation.
assumptions.applies_when: Used to scale an NPS-wide August 2026 recreation-visit total to Yellowstone. Transfers only if Yellowstone's relative share of NPS-wide August visitation in 2026 is similar to its historical share.
assumptions.falsified_by: Direct evidence that Yellowstone's August share of NPS-wide August visits is outside 0.8-1.8%, or a major Yellowstone-specific shock in August 2026 that decouples it from the NPS-wide total.

assumptions.name: Year-over-year change factor for NPS-wide August recreation visits, 2026 vs 2025
assumptions.rationale: No kept point provides a 2026 NPS-wide August total or a forecast. A neutral central value of 1.0 with a +/-10% range reflects typical year-over-year variation in NPS-wide visitation and the absence of specific 2026 information.
assumptions.applies_when: Used to project NPS-wide August 2025 recreation visits forward to August 2026. Transfers only if 2026 NPS-wide August visitation is broadly similar to 2025.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence of a large national travel shock, NPS-wide policy change, or a preliminary 2026 NPS-wide August total outside the 0.9-1.1 range.

methods.rationale: Base-rate route: use a comparable large western park's 2025 annual recreation visits (p42, Grand Teton) as a scale anchor, then apply Yellowstone's August share of annual visits (a1). This is a weak transfer because Grand Teton is not Yellowstone; it is retained only as a structural cross-check, not as a primary estimate. Shared dependency: both the anchor and the share are historical and assume no major August 2026 disruption.

Top-down route: take the 2025 NPS-wide annual recreation-visit total (p34), apply Yellowstone's share of NPS-wide visits (a2), then apply the August share of the annual total (a3). This assumes 2026 NPS-wide visitation is similar to 2025 and that both shares are stable. Failure modes: a 2026 NPS-wide surge or decline, a Yellowstone-specific shock, or a change in NPS reporting scope would break the transfer.

assumptions.name: Yellowstone August share of annual recreation visits
assumptions.rationale: Yellowstone's summer peak is concentrated in July-August; the August share of annual recreation visits has historically been in the mid-to-high teens. The range spans plausible recent values and is used only to scale an annual total to August.
assumptions.applies_when: A credible 2026 annual Yellowstone recreation-visit total is available or can be forecast, and August 2026 is not disrupted by a major closure or policy change relative to the annual pattern.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that Yellowstone's August share of annual visits has moved outside roughly 14-20% in recent years, or a major August-specific disruption that changes the seasonal distribution.

assumptions.name: Yellowstone share of NPS-wide annual recreation visits
assumptions.rationale: Yellowstone is one of the largest parks but its annual visits are a small share of the roughly 323 million NPS-wide total; the range reflects plausible recent shares consistent with the park's scale relative to the Top-10 parks listed.
assumptions.applies_when: An NPS-wide 2026 annual recreation-visit total or forecast is available and Yellowstone's relative share is stable.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that Yellowstone's share of NPS-wide visits has shifted materially outside the stated range, or that NPS-wide reporting scope changed.

assumptions.name: August share of NPS-wide annual recreation visits
assumptions.rationale: Summer months dominate NPS-wide visitation; August is typically one of the highest months. The range is a broad prior for the August share of the annual NPS-wide total.
assumptions.applies_when: An NPS-wide 2026 annual total is available and the August seasonal share is stable.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that the NPS-wide August share of annual visits falls outside roughly 10-14%.

methods.label: m1
methods.rationale: Base-rate route: use a comparable large western park's 2025 annual recreation visits (p42, Grand Teton) as a scale anchor, then apply Yellowstone's August share of annual visits (a1). This is a weak transfer because Grand Teton is not Yellowstone; it is retained only as a structural cross-check, not as a primary estimate. Shared dependency: both the anchor and the share are historical and assume n

methods.label: m2
methods.rationale: Top-down route: take the 2025 NPS-wide annual recreation-visit total (p34), apply Yellowstone's share of NPS-wide visits (a2), then apply the August share of the annual total (a3). This assumes 2026 NPS-wide visitation is similar to 2025 and that both shares are stable. kept.name: Yellowstone August share of annual recreation visits
kept.rationale: Yellowstone's summer peak is concentrated in July-August; the August share of annual recreation visits has historically been in the mid-to-high teens. The range spans plausible recent values and is used only to scale an annual total to August.
kept.applies_when: A credible 2026 annual Yellowstone recreation-visit total is available or can be forecast, and August 2026 is not disrupted by a major closure or policy change relative to the annual pattern.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence that Yellowstone's August share of annual visits has moved outside roughly 14-20% in recent years, or a major August-specific disruption that changes the seasonal distribution.

kept.name: Yellowstone share of NPS-wide annual recreation visits
kept.rationale: Yellowstone is one of the largest parks but its annual visits are a small share of the roughly 323 million NPS-wide total; the range reflects plausible recent shares consistent with the park's scale relative to the Top-10 parks listed.
kept.applies_when: An NPS-wide 2026 annual recreation-visit total or forecast is available and Yellowstone's relative share is stable.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence that Yellowstone's share of NPS-wide visits has shifted materially outside the stated range, or that NPS-wide reporting scope changed.

kept.name: August share of NPS-wide annual recreation visits
kept.rationale: Summer months dominate NPS-wide visitation; August is typically one of the highest months. The range is a broad prior for the August share of the annual NPS-wide total.
kept.applies_when: An NPS-wide 2026 annual total is available and the August seasonal share is stable.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence that the NPS-wide August share of annual visits falls outside roughly 10-14%.

residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.

ablation.rule: exclude points from own_history directions and points whose name contains a target entity anchor and whose name or unit shares a stem with the target unit (triangulate/agent/ablation.py)
residual_risks: Own values named by an alias or abbreviation, or with no entity in the point name, are not excluded.

The rule over-excludes on purpose: any point naming the target entity together with the target quantity (for example a survey of the target's visitors) is excluded, even when it is not a value of the target itself.
The model's own memory of the target's history is not removed: it can still shape the plan, the judge's choices and assumption values.
The searcher and the extractor still see pages that contain own values; only the judge's table is filtered.
